Transcript:Memory of Seren.wikitext:
{{Transcript|npc}}

==Grand Library Seals==
===Seal of the Forgotten===
...Therein lies my guilt. A part of me, trapped and alone. Dark, yes, but still a part of my being, sealed away in the Temple of Light. The protections on the temple, they should keep her contained. But in case they don't, I created one last safeguard, a prison within a prison. With it I made a key, an orb of light, to unlock the darkness. I could have destroyed it, sealed her away forever. But I still question my decision, so I hid the orb away, while I think upon my choices. The shrine at Gorlah, that is where it lies. With it, she can be freed... or destroyed...

===Seal of Ithell===
When I first encountered the elves on their homeworld of Tarddiad, it was like I had finally found my purpose. I quickly fell in love with them, and they with me. I set out to help them, to guide them. They immediately embraced this, and one of their mystics, Ceidwad, documented my teachings in a great book called the Cerddi. It was the start of something beautiful, but there is pain in beauty, as I soon came to realise...

===Seal of Cadarn===
...Compared to many of the mortal races I had encountered, the elves had reasonable lifespans. And yet, it wasn't long enough. As I spent time with the elves, I watched as they withered and died. Each death was a blade through my heart, but none more so than Ceidwad, my closest companion. It didn't seem fair, didn't seem right. They deserved more. I knew I had to give it to them...

===Seal of Crwys===
...I found a way to share my essence with the elves, a piece of my being for each one of them. With this gift, their years would number in the thousands, time enough to live the lives they deserved. In keeping with elven tradition, the gift was given through a song. They called it the song of creation, for it was the creation of a new life for them. At least, so we thought...

===Seal of Amlodd===
...With all my knowledge, I should have known not to meddle. That which I intended as a gift, soon turned out to be their curse. The song of creation increased their lifespans, but at a terrible price. It bound them to me. To stray too far from their sides, caused pain, and even death. I knew I had to help them, to fix my mistakes. I should have known that I'd only make it worse...

===Seal of Meilyr===
...Another being came to our world. Divine like myself, but not by design. He spoke of a perfect world, one filled with power. I knew it was a risk, but I decided to travel there. The power he spoke of might have been the only thing capable of saving the elves. The curse made it impossible for me to go without them, so they had to come with me, and leave their home behind. It was hard on them, but in the end, I managed to convince them...

===Seal of Hefin===
...We made our home in the new world, in a great city of crystal spires. It was as beautiful as the world from which we came. But beneath that beauty, the curse remained. The power that filled the world was even greater than I had anticipated. A higher power, one I had not encountered for a long time. I was sure this world held the key to breaking the curse, I just needed to find it...

===Seal of Traehaern===
...It took millennia, but I finally made a breakthrough. Deep beneath the mountains near our home, I found a source of deathly energy. I was sure I could use this power to save them. My essence is of life, of light. This darkness would be the perfect counter, a way to nullify the curse. I should have known not to be so foolish. This curse started with my meddling, my meddling was never going to end it...

===Seal of Iorwerth===
...I am a being of light, but even within me, there was some darkness. I poured this darkness into my creation, combining it with the deathly energy I had found. When I was done, I looked upon my creation. A fragment of myself, but one of darkness, rather than light. I though her essence would counter my own, ending the curse with her mere existence. It was not to be though. The curse was tied to me, not to her. I had failed, and she knew it. She turned on me, tried to destroy me. I had to stop her, so I sealed her away, in the very place I had created her...

==Memoriam device==
===Memoriam crystal 1===
I have tried to convince him to stay, but he will not listen. He believes our mother is controlling us, keeping us close against our will. He does not see that she only acts out of fear, fear that she might lose us. He wants me to join him, but I won't leave her behind. She is our mother, our creator, we owe everything to her.

===Memoriam crystal 2===
She cries out for him, desperate for him to return to her. I've been trying my best to comfort her, but it has been little help. In her desperation for him to return, she has created new life in his image. They are pale imitations though, shadows of him and I. Their creation has been sapping her energy, and I fear she will grow too weak. All may not be lost though, for I may be able to convince them to sacrifice their energy and return it to her.

===Memoriam crystal 3===
She has been dreaming more and more often recently. As she dreams, more beings are manifested. While her initial creations held some intellect, the latest ones have been purely instinctual. She is clearly running out of energy and running out of time. The beings that sacrificed themselves for her slowed things down, but it hasn't been enough. I am left with no choice, for I am powerless to help her. I have to leave her, before it is too late.

===Memoriam crystal 4===
It was not easy to leave her, but I knew I had no choice. Since my departure, I travelled far and wide, finding nothing but empty worlds, long since abandoned. I almost gave up, but just as I was ready to stop, I came upon a world full of life. The creatures here, they are a joy to behold, living in harmony with each other and their home. I approached them, fearful of how they would react to me. It soon became clear that there was no need for fear. They fell in love with me, and I fell in love with them. At long last, I feel like I am home. Never shall I leave their side.

* '''Mord Gunnars:''' Hail the conquering hero!

* {{topt|Tell me more about Jatizso's history.}}
** '''Player:''' Tell me more about Jatizso.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' Well now, the history of the isles is a bloody tale. When told in its intended form it takes 9 days and 9 nights. However, I will give you the abridged version.
** '''Player:''' Phew!
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' Four generations ago there was a mighty king who ruled wisely and was loved by all.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' He had many sons, most of whom proved themselves in the usual Fremennik ways of fighting, sailing, drinking and so on.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' His youngest two sons, however, were a problem. Ever since they were old enough to hit one another they had bickered and fought.
** '''Maria Gunnars:''' Their names were Jatizso and Neitiznot.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' Hey! Who's telling this story?
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' Ahem. At the time it was customary for the Kings' sons to claim a prize from his treasury when they came of age.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' Each brother rallied support and strode out to confront the other on the field of battle to claim the same prize.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' The brothers met on the field, limbs were bruised, bones were crushed and heads clashed.
** '''Maria Gunnars:''' They probably didn't notice the head-clashing bit. Too thick skulled!
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' Can I finish the story without interruptions?
** '''Maria Gunnars:''' Carry on dear.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' Anyway, long into the night they fought, until they stood alone, facing each other.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' On the second day the old king, whose patience was exhausted, strode out onto the field and demanded to know who had claimed his prize.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' Jatizso looked at his father and told him yes, it was his, to which the other called out 'No! It's not'.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' And so, the argument continued through to the third day, with the sounds of 'Jah! 'tis so!', 'Ne! It's not!' echoing over the field, becoming more hoarse as the darkness enveloped the brothers.
** '''Maria Gunnars:''' Bah! What they needed was a good clip round the ear.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' At the end of the third day, when the brothers lay unable to move, let alone stand, the King stood between them in shame.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' As punishment for their squabbling he banished his sons from his realm, ordering that neither should return until they had conquered lands of their own.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' Jatizso set sail with a band of loyal followers, sailing into the east, while Neitiznot went west.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' Jatizso ventured far into uncharted oceans, his crew dwindling as the trials of sailing and sea monsters took them.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' Jatizso's ship limped through the frozen wastes, in need of repairs, fighting off pirates who thought them easy pickings.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' At last a promising land was sighted, a land rich in minerals, deep fjords and sweeping mountains.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' Jatizso claimed the land and named it after himself.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' A mighty citadel was constructed to protect his land; then Jatizso set forth to explore his new kingdom.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' Crossing a few fjords, Jatizso spied an island which remained green and fertile, even at such latitude.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' With a mighty cheer Jatizso and his men marched on the island. Upon reaching the island, however, they discovered a wooden stockade.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' Determined to be master of all the land, Jatizso stood in front of the gates. He looked up and demanded that those within the stockade surrendered.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' Jatizso was horrified when his brother appeared on the battlements and cried 'This is my land! Go find yer own'. To which his brother replied 'No it's not!', throwing some rocks for good measure.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' And so the blood feud continued.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' The fighting between the towns has continued for generations with little sign of improvement.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' Quite recently a massive troll army seized one of the islands to the north, while our townships' militias were busy fighting one another.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' They marched down and razed Neitiznot to the ground while Neitiznot's troops laid siege to Jatizso.
** '''Maria Gunnars:''' The smoke damage was atrocious, I had to replace my entire wardrobe.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' Yes, dear.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' Anyway, a hasty sort of peace has been agreed until the trolls are dealt with.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' But you can still see the bitter rivalry as guards hurl insults between the towns.
** {{tact|previous}}
* {{topt|Tell me more about the King of Jatizso.}}
** '''Player:''' Tell me more about the King of Jatizso.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' Ha! Our benevolent King Gjuki Sorvott IV.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' He is short-tempered, arrogant and cares little about anything except outdoing Neitiznot's Burgher.
** '''Maria:''' He's not at all like Burgher Burowgar.
** '''Mord Gunnars:''' I'm surprised King Sorvott wishes to talk to you. Don't expect much in the way of gratitude.

** '''Natural historian:''' A tiny, light-sensitive, transparent structure on top of the head that helps them regulate how long they stay in the sun.
** '''Natural historian:''' This is vital for the cold-blooded lizards who have no means to regulate their internal temperature.
** '''Natural historian:''' Like many cold-blooded creatures, if they are subjected to a sudden decrease in temperature, they will become sluggish and sleepy.
** '''Natural historian:''' And this concludes my short lecture on lizards. I hope you've enjoyed yourselves.
** {{Qact|End cutscene}}
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Tell me about tortoises.}}
** '''Player:''' Tell me about the tortoises.
** '''Natural historian:''' Ahh tortoises, the armoured ancients.
** '''Natural historian:''' If you just follow me to the display case I shall explain all about them.
** {{Qact|The player and the natural historian teleport to a cutscene in front of the tortoise display case with a teacher and pupil and schoolgirl.}}
** '''Natural historian:''' The tortoise is a very well defended beast. It uses an armoured shell just like its aquatic cousins the terrapin and the turtle.
** {{Qact|The natural historian poses as a tortoise...}} <!-- Repeatedly -->
** '''Natural historian:''' Tortoises can vary in size from about as long as your hand to as big as a unicorn. Most land tortoises eat nothing but plants in the wild.
** '''Natural historian:''' Did you know you can tell how old a tortoise is by the number of rings in its shell, just like a tree.
** '''Natural historian:''' Most land-based tortoises eat plants, feeding on grazing grasses, weeds, leafy greens, flowers, and cabbages.
** '''Natural historian:''' Tortoises generally live as long as people, and some individual ones are known to have lived longer than 300 years.
** '''Natural historian:''' Because of this, they symbolise longevity within some cultures, such as gnomes who also breed them for battle.
** '''Natural historian:''' The oldest tortoise ever recorded was Mibbiwocket, who was presented to the King Healthorg the Great, by the famous explorer Admiral Bake, shortly after its birth.
** '''Natural historian:''' Mibbiwocket is still in the care of the gnomish royal family.
** '''Natural historian:''' And this concludes my short lecture on tortoises. I hope you've enjoyed yourselves.
** {{Qact|End cutscene}}
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Tell me about dragons.}}
** '''Player:''' Tell me about dragons.
** '''Natural historian:''' Ahh dragons, the mighty hunters of the sky.
** '''Natural historian:''' If you just follow me to the display case I shall explain all about them.
** {{Qact|The player and the natural historian teleport to a cutscene in front of the dragon display case with a teacher and pupil.}}
** '''Natural historian:''' The dragons of Gielinor are a most confusing species. Standing at approximately twelve feet tall, these imposing predators strike fear into the hearts and minds of most sane folk.
** {{Qact|The natural historian poses as a dragon...}} <!-- Repeatedly -->
** '''Natural historian:''' However, if you delve a little deeper into their history and lifestyle, a few things stick out as very unusual.
** '''Natural historian:''' With most species there is a line, an ancestry if you will, whereby you can track how a creature has come to be in its present form.
** '''Natural historian:''' For instance, you can trace the ancestry of the common house cat back to the same creature that became the sabre-toothed kyatt.
** '''Natural historian:''' However, with the dragon, no such root ancestor can be found.
** '''Natural historian:''' There are many forms of dragon, such as the common coloured and the metallic, or ferrous, dragon.
** '''Natural historian:''' They colonise many areas of Gielinor, though most notably, sites of ancient battles and small dank caves.
** '''Natural historian:''' Eating habits tend to vary, with the majority of their food being meat. However, it has also been noted that they can consume metals just as easily, with runite being thought of as a delicacy.
** '''Natural historian:''' Throughout history, dragons have appeared in myth and legend as fearsome adversaries and cunning creatures.
** '''Natural historian:''' However, modern evidence does not support this. Most young dragons are largely creatures of instinct with a strong vicious streak.
** '''Natural historian:''' The lifespan of the common dragon is as yet unknown, as no dragon has ever been observed dying of old age.
** '''Natural historian:''' Although, it has been mooted that spontaneous combustion could be considered a natural cause of death for this species.
** '''Natural historian:''' And this concludes my short lecture on dragons. I hope you've enjoyed yourselves.
** {{Qact|End cutscene}}
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Tell me about wyverns.}}
** '''Player:''' Tell me about the wyverns.
** '''Natural historian:''' Ahh, wyverns. The extinct lizards.
** '''Natural historian:''' If you just follow me to the display case I shall explain all about them.
** {{Qact|The player and the natural historian teleport to a cutscene in front of the wyvern display case with a teacher and pupil and schoolgirl.}}
** '''Natural historian:''' The wyverns' tale is a sad one. This now extinct species is presumed in some way to be related to the dragon.
** {{Qact|The natural historian poses as a wyvern...}} <!-- Repeatedly -->
** '''Natural historian:''' In that they are both large flying reptiles. The wyvern stands much shorter than the adult dragon and only has two legs as opposed to the dragon's four.
** '''Natural historian:''' Much of the evidence for wyvern behaviour comes from the reconstruction of old bones in the icy mountains of Asgarnia.
** '''Natural historian:''' One is that Asgarnia was at one time a much more temperate climate than it is now. The other is that wyverns could generate fire internally in much the same way as dragons.
** '''Natural historian:''' If they follow the dragon paradigm, then they would have been carnivores, feeding on cows, sheep and other livestock animals.
** '''Natural historian:''' How and why the wyverns became extinct is something of a mystery. Though if you consider the theory that the climate of Asgarnia changed suddenly, then this could provide an explanation.
** '''Natural historian:''' There are some inconsistencies in the findings we have for the wyverns, such as the odd wear patterns of some of bones, which really could only have happened after the creature died.
** '''Natural historian:''' Also the bones we have collected remain a little below room temperature wherever they are kept.
** '''Natural historian:''' They have also been shown to radiate a very weak magical aura.
** '''Natural historian:''' I'm sure that in due time, these mysteries will be solved.
** '''Natural historian:''' And this concludes my short lecture on wyverns. I hope you've enjoyed yourselves.
** {{Qact|End cutscene}}
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|That's enough education for one day.}}
** '''Player:''' That's enough education for one day.
** '''Natural historian:''' Nonsense! There's always room for more.
** '''Natural historian:''' And remember, science isn't dull!
** {{tact|end}}

** '''Natural historian:''' Ahh snails, the gelatinous gastropods.

** {{Qact|The player and the natural historian teleport to a cutscene in front of the snail display case with a schoolboy and schoolgirl.}}
** '''Natural historian:''' Snails move like worms by squishing up and stretching out, very, very slowly. They also make a lot of slime, in order to aid moving by reducing friction.
** {{Qact|The natural historian poses as a snail...}} <!-- Repeatedly -->
** '''Natural historian:''' They also use slime for protection. For instance, snails can use their slime to crawl over razor-blades without being hurt. It also helps keep away dangerous insects like ants.
** '''Natural historian:''' When they hide in their shells, snails secrete a special type of slime, which dries to cover the entrance of their shells like a 'trapdoor'. This is called an operculum.
** '''Natural historian:''' The snails of Morytania are the most malignant molluscs ever to have been studied.
** '''Natural historian:''' They are broken down into two distinct species: achatina acidia and achatina acidia giganteus or, as they are more commonly known, the acid-spitting snail and the giant acid-spitting snail.
** '''Natural historian:''' Both of these varieties are voracious carnivores, using their mutated mouthpieces to spit a glob of powerful acid to kill their foe.
** '''Natural historian:''' They then simply have to wait, whilst the digestive juices make short work of the poor creature. Then, they simply slurp up what remains.
** '''Natural historian:''' How these strange creatures came to be is still something of a mystery. The most prevalent theory suggests that they mutated, as a reaction to an 'as yet unknown' pollutant that has appeared in the swamps.
** '''Natural historian:''' The local populace has capitalised on the appearance of these strange species, using their shells to fashion a rudimentary helm that is fairly resistant to the snails acid.
** '''Natural historian:''' Other known uses of snail by-products include a tasty local delicacy and a fireproof oil.
** '''Natural historian:''' And this concludes my short lecture on snails. I hope you've enjoyed yourselves.
** {{Qact|End cutscene}}
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Tell me about monkeys.}}
** '''Player:''' Tell me about monkeys.
** '''Natural historian:''' Ahh monkeys, the simian collective.
** '''Natural historian:''' If you just follow me to the display case I shall explain all about them.
** {{Qact|The player and the natural historian teleport to a cutscene in front of the monkey display case with a teacher and pupil and schoolboy.}}
** '''Natural historian:''' A monkey is a member of either of two known groupings of simian primates. These two known groupings are the Karamja monkeys and the 'harmless' monkeys.
** {{Qact|The natural historian poses as a monkey...}} <!-- Repeatedly -->
** '''Natural historian:''' Because of their similarity to monkeys, apes such as chimpanzees and gibbons are often called monkeys by accident.
** '''Natural historian:''' Though some natural historians don't consider them to be monkeys. Also, a few monkey species have the word 'ape' in their common name.
** '''Natural historian:''' The Karamja monkeys are rumoured to be fairly cunning and intelligent creatures, although rumours that they have learned human speech is anecdotal at best.
** '''Natural historian:''' In appearance, they stand much shorter than a human and tend to move in a hunched fashion. Karamja monkeys also sport a red mohawk, though it is unknown whether this is an affectation or not.
** '''Natural historian:''' They are very fond of bananas and bitternuts, eating them in huge quantities whenever they can get their paws on them.
** '''Natural historian:''' The harmless monkeys of Mos Le'Harmless are a very similar, but in some ways entirely different, breed. They stand roughly the same size but are a lighter colour.
** '''Natural historian:''' Interestingly, Karamaja monkeys have a deep dislike of seaweed, though this may stem from the actions of a number of irresponsible people.
** '''Natural historian:''' And this concludes my short lecture on monkeys. I hope you've enjoyed yourselves.
** {{Qact|End cutscene}}
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Tell me about sea slugs.}}
** '''Player:''' Tell me about the sea slugs.
** '''Natural historian:''' Ahh sea slugs, the cute crustaceans.
** '''Natural historian:''' If you just follow me to the display case I shall explain all about them.
** {{Qact|The player and the natural historian teleport to a cutscene in front of the sea slug display case with a teacher and pupil and schoolgirl.}}
** '''Natural historian:''' The term 'sea slug' is something of a misnomer. Whilst these small creatures have a soft body like that of a slug, they also possess a very hard shell like a snail.
** {{Qact|The natural historian poses as a sea slug...}} <!-- Repeatedly -->
** '''Natural historian:''' Very little is actually known about the sea slug, as we have, as yet, been unable to procure a sample for observation and study.
** '''Natural historian:''' For some reason all expeditions we have sent have either vanished mysteriously, or those on the expedition have sent letters back announcing their desire to leave the Museum and go on to other things.
** '''Natural historian:''' It is presumed that the species is native to the very deep waters around the eastern Ardougne coastline.
** '''Natural historian:''' There must be some natural resource in the area that the sea slugs are using, as the underwater habitat there is much the same around many coastal areas on Gielinor.
** '''Natural historian:''' Through looking at similar species we have determined that the sea slug is a harmless little creature. It spends much of its life grazing on seaweed and other plant life.
** '''Natural historian:''' There are reports that these reclusive animals have two large fangs at their front, though this is assumed to be either for decorative or defensive purposes.
** '''Natural historian:''' If they do follow the same pattern as other similar creatures, the shell will be nigh on impervious to most attacks. The exposed soft skin may have a number of nematocysts, or stinging organs, similar to jellyfish.
** '''Natural historian:''' It is typical of prey animals such as these to develop some kind of unique defence mechanism that allows them to survive.
** '''Natural historian:''' If only we could acquire one for study. I'm sure we would find this mechanism to be truly unique.
** '''Natural historian:''' And this concludes my short lecture on sea slugs. I hope you've enjoyed yourselves.
** {{Qact|End cutscene}}
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Tell me about snakes.}}
** '''Player:''' Tell me about snakes.
** '''Natural historian:''' Ahh snakes, the slithering squamata.
** '''Natural historian:''' If you just follow me to the display case I shall explain all about them.
** {{Qact|The player and the natural historian teleport to a cutscene in front of the snake display case with a teacher and pupil and schoolgirl.}}
** '''Natural historian:''' Serpentes, or ophidia, is the suborder under squamata that snakes belong to, like a big family.
** {{Qact|The natural historian poses as a snake...}} <!-- Repeatedly -->
** '''Natural historian:''' Unlike lizards, snakes have no limbs whatsoever; not that this limits them. Snakes live in or near every habitat in the world.
** '''Natural historian:''' Found in nice tropical forests, temperate lattitudes and even in the ocean - some have adapted specialised stomach juices that they inject into their prey as venom, while others prefer to grab and crush their food.
** '''Natural historian:''' While others still are fast hunters who use speed and strength to overcome their prey.
** '''Natural historian:''' The sense of smell in snakes has been enhanced in an amazing way. With most animals, like you and me, tiny particles are filtered through the nose.
** '''Natural historian:''' However, instead of using just their nose, these animals use their tongues as well. When a lizard or a snake wants to smell it's surroundings, it will wave its tongue around and pick up the particles in the air.
** '''Natural historian:''' The tongue then returns to the mouth and the tips of the tongue are pushed up against two tiny pits in the roof of the snake's mouth.
** '''Natural historian:''' Since these pits are split apart from each other, the tongue itself also has to split. This is why snakes have forked tongues.
** '''Natural historian:''' So the next time you see a snake sticking it's tongue out at you, remember, it's sniffing the air, not trying to bite you.
** '''Natural historian:''' And this concludes my short lecture on snakes. I hope you've enjoyed yourselves.
** {{Qact|End cutscene}}
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|That's enough education for one day.}}
** {{tact|above}}

==Dialogue in the southern section==
* '''Natural historian:''' Hello again, [sir/madam], how can I help you on this fine day?
* '''Player:''' I was hoping you could tell me about something.

* {{topt|Tell me about natural history.}}
** '''Player:''' Tell me about natural history.
** '''Natural historian:''' Well, the field of natural history covers a wide range of sciences.
** '''Natural historian:''' So we use biology, the study of living things, botany, the study of plants and zoology, the study of animals.
** '''Natural historian:''' Though the field is growing all the time and we're also using techniques from magic, astrology and numerology.
** '''Natural historian:''' A person interested in natural history is known as a naturalist.
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Tell me about terrorbirds.}}
** '''Player:''' Tell me about the terrorbirds.
** '''Natural historian:''' Ahh terrorbirds, the fastest bird on two legs.
** '''Natural historian:''' If you just follow me to the display case I shall explain all about them.
** {{Qact|The player and the natural historian teleport to a cutscene in front of the terrorbird display case with a teacher and pupil and schoolgirl.}}
** '''Natural historian:''' Terrorbirds live in nomadic groups of between five and fifty birds that often travel together with other grazing animals.
** {{Qact|The natural historian poses as a terrorbird...}} <!-- Repeatedly -->
** '''Natural historian:''' They mainly feed on seeds and other plants. They also eat insects such as locusts if they can catch them.
** '''Natural historian:''' They have no teeth to chew with, so they swallow pebbles that help to grind the swallowed foods in the gizzard.
** '''Natural historian:''' They can go without water for a long time, exclusively living off the water in the plants. However, they enjoy water and frequently take baths when they can.
** '''Natural historian:''' Terrorbirds are known to eat almost anything, particularly in captivity, where opportunity is increased.
** '''Natural historian:''' Terrorbirds usually weigh a little less than a small unicorn. The feathers of adult males are mostly green, with some white on the wings and tail.
** '''Natural historian:''' There are claws on two of the wings' fingers and their strong legs have no feathers. The bird stands on two toes, with the bigger one resembling a hoof. Its feet have no claws.
** '''Natural historian:''' This is an adaptation unique to terrorbirds that appears to aid in running. Their legs are powerful enough to kill even large animals.
** '''Natural historian:''' The gnomes in particular, prize the terrorbird for its fast running speed, using them as mounts whenever possible.
** '''Natural historian:''' There are a number of recorded incidents of people being attacked and killed. Big males can be very territorial and aggressive, and can attack and kick very powerfully with their legs.
** '''Natural historian:''' A terrorbird is so fast, it can easily outrun any human athlete.
** '''Natural historian:''' And this concludes my short lecture on terrorbirds. I hope you've enjoyed yourselves.
** {{Qact|End cutscene}}
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Tell me about the Kalphite Queen.}}
** '''Player:''' Tell me about the Kalphite Queen.
** '''Natural historian:''' Ahh kalphites, the insectoid eating machines.
** '''Natural historian:''' If you just follow me to the display case I shall explain all about them.
** {{Qact|The player and the natural historian teleport to a cutscene in front of the Kalphite Queen display case with a teacher and pupil and schoolgirl.}}
** '''Natural historian:''' The kalphites, otherwise known as the kalphiscarabeinae, are perhaps the largest species of insect on the face of Gielinor. Their queen is called kalphiscarabeinae pasha.
** {{Qact|The natural historian poses as the Kalphite Queen...}} <!-- Repeatedly -->
** '''Natural historian:''' Most of the early documentation and research on this fearsome predatory species was performed by the noted bug hunter Iqbar Ali-Abdula.
** '''Natural historian:''' This, of course, was before he was driven insane by his research and ran off into the desert, screaming.
** '''Natural historian:''' Kalphites are related to beetles and scorpions; they are mainly green in colour. Some have remarkable antennae which can detect the slightest movement. Their carapace is composed of armoured plates called lamellae.
** '''Natural historian:''' This shell can be compressed into a ball or fanned out like leaves, in order to sense odours. The front legs are adapted for digging the enormous tunnel systems that serve as their nests.
** '''Natural historian:''' They exist in a caste-based society, with the soft shelled larvae at the bottom, up through the workers, soldiers and finally the queen.
** '''Natural historian:''' Voracious carnivores, a pack of adult workers can strip the flesh from a full grown camel in a matter of seconds, leaving nothing but a few bones and strips of fur for other scavengers to pick over.
** '''Natural historian:''' They typically live in large nests marked by the rock hard pillars found in hot, arid deserts, such as the one south-west of Al Kharid, which rise out of the sands like the tombs of desert pharaohs.
** '''Natural historian:''' Indeed, there is some relationship between the Kalphite Queen and the desert god Scabaras, but no one is really sure what.
** '''Natural historian:''' During the early part of the fourth age, Scabaras proclaimed himself omnipotent and outlawed worship of all other gods save him.
** '''Natural historian:''' When the people eventually revolted against his repressive rule and banished Scabaras, it is said his blood washed over the scarabs and transformed them into the kalphites we know today.
** '''Natural historian:''' Of course, any right-minded scientist discounts these myths as mere stories, with no historical basis in fact.
** '''Natural historian:''' And this concludes my short lecture on kalphites. I hope you've enjoyed yourselves.
** {{Qact|End cutscene}}
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|That's enough education for one day.}}
** {{tact|above}}

==Dialogue in the western section==
* '''Natural historian:''' Hello again, [sir/madam], how can I help you on this fine day?
* '''Player:''' I was hoping you could tell me about something.

* {{topt|Tell me about camels.}}
** '''Player:''' Tell me about camels.
** '''Natural historian:''' Ahh camels, the ships of the desert.
** '''Natural historian:''' If you just follow me to the display case I shall explain all about them.
** {{Qact|The player and the natural historian teleport to a cutscene in front of the camel display case with a teacher and pupil and schoolgirl.}}
** '''Natural historian:''' The term camel refers to either of the two known species of camelid.
** {{Qact|The natural historian poses as a camel...}} <!-- Repeatedly -->
** '''Natural historian:''' There is the bactrian, which has two humps and can be found throughout Al Kharid. It also refers to the Ugthanki, or one-humped camel.
** '''Natural historian:''' Camels are ill-tempered beasts at the best of times, requiring a great deal of time and effort to tame.
** '''Natural historian:''' This would explain why used camel salesmen are in such a hurry to be rid of them.
** '''Natural historian:''' In the wild, camels have been known to lie in wait and ambush hapless travellers, before devouring them.
** '''Natural historian:''' This is quite surprising, as most domestic camels are happy eating nothing but vegetables.
** '''Natural historian:''' Camel milk is much more nutritious than cow milk and goes well in the strong desert drink akin to tea.
** '''Natural historian:''' Another useful camel by-product is dung. Their dung is very dry, due to the highly efficient metabolism of the camel.
** '''Natural historian:''' Scientific research has also shown that chilli has a disastrous effect on a camel's digestive system, which produces toxic dung.
** '''Natural historian:''' And this concludes my short lecture on camels. I hope you've enjoyed yourselves.
** {{Qact|End cutscene}}
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Tell me about leeches.}}
** '''Player:''' Tell me about leeches.
** '''Natural historian:''' Ahh leeches, the haemophagic parasites.
** '''Natural historian:''' If you just follow me to the display case I shall explain all about them.
** {{Qact|The player and the natural historian teleport to a cutscene in front of the leech display case with a teacher and pupil and schoolgirl.}}
** '''Natural historian:''' Leeches are fascinating creatures and are very similar to worms in most respects.
** {{Qact|The natural historian poses as a leech...}} <!-- Repeatedly -->
** '''Natural historian:''' They like to inhabit streams, rivers and seas, but their preference is for stagnant pools of water.
** '''Natural historian:''' One of the most common misconceptions is that all leeches feed on blood.
** '''Natural historian:''' Most leeches are meat eaters, feeding on a variety of invertebrates such as worms, snails, insect larvae and snails.
** '''Natural historian:''' Those that do feed on blood have developed an amazing method of doing so. Firstly they latch onto the skin using a ring of tiny teeth, before injecting their prey with an anaesthetic.
** '''Natural historian:''' Then they bite into the skin using a Y-shaped mouthpiece and introducing a chemical that stops the blood from clotting.
** '''Natural historian:''' They will then feed until they are completely full, sometimes doubling in size!
** '''Natural historian:''' Most leeches are very small, measuring no more than the length of your middle finger. An exception to these are the leeches of Morytania, which can reach the size of a dog.
** '''Natural historian:''' They are much more mobile than their smaller cousins and are able to jump rather high when attacking.
** '''Natural historian:''' Quite how these leeches came to be so big is something of a mystery.
** '''Natural historian:''' All we can assume is that there is some kind of environmental influence, which has governed their immense growth.
** '''Natural historian:''' And this concludes my short lecture on leeches. I hope you've enjoyed yourselves.
** {{Qact|End cutscene}}
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Tell me about moles.}}
** '''Player:''' Tell me about moles.
** '''Natural historian:''' Ahh moles, the mammalian mountain makers.
** '''Natural historian:''' If you just follow me to the display case I shall explain all about them.
** {{Qact|The player and the natural historian teleport to a cutscene in front of the mole display case with a teacher and pupil and schoolgirl.}}
** '''Natural historian:''' Now, moles are small mammals of the talpidae family. These subterranean burrowers mainly live on a diet of slugs, snails and insects.
** {{Qact|The natural historian poses as a mole...}} <!-- Repeatedly -->
** '''Natural historian:''' They vary greatly in habitat and can be found in almost every part of Gielinor. Some species have even known to be aquatic!
** '''Natural historian:''' Male moles are known as boars with the females called sows. Should you come across a group of moles, you would call them a labour.
** '''Natural historian:''' Moles are considered to be an agricultural pest in most places, digging up the ground and leaving molehills all over the place.
** '''Natural historian:''' This has been highlighted in Falador by Wyson the Gardener who, after using some Malignus Mortifer's Super Ultra Flora Growth Potion, managed to create Gielinor's only known species of giant mole.
** '''Natural historian:''' This fearsome beast has huge claws, wicked teeth and a penchant for shiny objects. It is a very tough animal with a thick protective hide and an ill temperament.
** '''Natural historian:''' That said, they do benefit the soil by aerating and tilling it, adding to its fertility. Contrary to popular belief, moles don't eat plant roots.
** '''Natural historian:''' And this concludes my short lecture on moles. I hope you've enjoyed yourselves.
** {{Qact|End cutscene}}
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|Tell me about penguins.}}
** '''Player:''' Tell me about penguins.
** '''Natural historian:''' Ahh penguins, the cunning birds of the sea.
** '''Natural historian:''' If you just follow me to the display case I shall explain all about them.
** {{Qact|The player and the natural historian teleport to a cutscene in front of the penguin display case with a teacher and pupil and schoolgirl.}}
** '''Natural historian:''' This often-maligned aquatic bird is known to be native to the ice fields of Etceteria, although they have been known to live as far as the fields of Lumbridge.
** {{Qact|The natural historian poses as a penguin...}} <!-- Repeatedly -->
** '''Natural historian:''' These aquatic birds seem to spend the majority of their time eating and fostering their young.
** '''Natural historian:''' For creatures with such small brains, they do seem to have a disproportionate capacity for forward thinking and planning. As this serves no natural purpose, scholars are divided as to how this evolved.
** '''Natural historian:''' Their diet consists mainly of fish, squid and a small shrimp-like creature called krill. However, some have developed a taste for the mushrooms that grow around fairy rings.
** '''Natural historian:''' Penguins primarily rely on their vision while hunting. What we don't know is how penguins locate prey in the darkness, or at great depths.
** '''Natural historian:''' Some theories suggest that penguins are helped by some sort of extra sensory perception; perhaps even precognition.
** '''Natural historian:''' Penguins spend a long time going without food when they are breeding. In fact, they won't even leave their nests if they can help it.
** '''Natural historian:''' Fortunately, most penguins build up a layer of fat to keep them warm and provide energy until the moult is over.
** '''Natural historian:''' And this concludes my short lecture on penguins. I hope you've enjoyed yourselves.
** {{Qact|End cutscene}}
** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|That's enough education for one day.}}
** {{tact|above}}

==Standard dialogue==
* '''Necto:''' Hello there! Looking to take advantage of the Mistrock mines? If so, I'm happy to buy any ores from you. I can also sell you some tools if needed.
* {{tselect|Select an option}}
* {{topt|Let's trade.}}
** '''Player:''' Let's trade.
** '''Necto:''' Great!
** {{tact|opens=Mistrock Mining Supplies}}
* {{topt|What can you tell me about this place?}}
** '''Player:''' What can you tell me about this place?
** '''Necto:''' Mistrock? It's a mining outpost. It was set up by Cam Torum after you humans went and had another of your wars. We lost some good mines and needed to find new ones.
** '''Player:''' Why here?
** '''Necto:''' It wasn't the first choice, but both humans and dwarves alike were pretty poor after the fighting ended, so we all had to learn lessons in how to compromise.
** '''Necto:''' Still, it ended up not being too bad in the end. We found there was a reasonable supply of coal and iron here, along with some silver and gold.
** '''Necto:''' The location ended up being quite appealing for some as well. It makes for a nice change of scenery for those that appreciate that sort of thing.
** '''Player:''' So what was here before Mistrock?
** '''Necto:''' Nothing much of note. The land here was owned by the Moonrise Brewery and Winery, but they found it wasn't much good for growing grapes.
** '''Player:''' So they were happy to give it up?
** '''Necto:''' Very happy. They saw an opportunity for a new business relationship. In return for giving us the land, we now give them favourable rates on what we mine here.

===Prior to A Tail of Two Cats===
* '''Player:''' Hello. What's your name?

* '''Player:''' Well, my name is [player name] and I'm pleased to meet you. So, now that I'm not a stranger anymore, what's your name?

* {{topt|How come you're the only cat around here?}}
** '''Player:''' How come you're the only cat around here?
** '''Neite:''' Oh there's far more than just me. The others are just shy. We do also get visitors from outside the city sometimes, like that Bob. He's quite a handsome beast...
** '''Player:''' Oh, I see. Romance is in the air, is it?
** '''Neite:''' Well, life here in the desert can be a lonely existence, even with all my busy work... Still, to be honest, he worries me.
** '''Player:''' In what way?
** '''Neite:''' Well, I pride myself on my knowledge of the family lines of cats. Obviously, Bob features quite heavily in most family trees, but he himself has none!
** '''Player:''' What do you mean?
** '''Neite:''' Nobody is sure where he came from. Not even the Sphinx knows. It's just one of those mysteries.
** '''Player:''' Interesting...
** {{tact|other}}
* {{topt|What are you doing?}}
** '''Player:''' What are you doing?
** '''Neite:''' I'm hunting frogs and locusts.
** '''Player:''' Why? Do they taste good?
** '''Neite:''' Yuck! No, I would never debase myself to eat such filth.
** '''Player:''' I see you're a cat of taste then.
** '''Neite:''' I am a cat of high breeding! My family tree dates back before those of any ruler on Gielinor.
** '''Player:''' What do you do with the frogs and locusts?
** '''Neite:''' What do you mean by 'do'?
** '''Player:''' Well, seeing as you're hunting them, I thought you'd eat them too.
** '''Neite:''' No, no, I just hunt them, play with them for a bit and then kill them.
** '''Player:''' Isn't that a little evil?
** '''Neite:''' What's evil about a little destruction?
** '''Player:''' What isn't? You destroy and take away life. What good is there in that?
** '''Neite:''' Life can come from destruction too. Take a volcano. It will destroy all life that surrounds it, but it will also fertilise and enrich the surrounding earth.
** '''Neite:''' From that earth, more life will spring forth than there was in the first place.
** '''Player:''' How do you compare killing frogs to a volcano? A volcano has no choice about whether it explodes or not, but you do have a choice.
** '''Neite:''' I disagree. It's in my nature to prey on smaller life forms in the same way as it is in the volcanoes nature to explode.
** '''Player:''' Don't they sometimes call the Devourer the goddess of destruction? You seem to have a lot in common with a goddess that your kind oppose.
** '''Neite:''' That is not too surprising. A long time ago, I served her. Her form has changed a lot since then, just as mine has.
** '''Player:''' You mean you weren't always a cat?
** '''Neite:''' No, I used to be human. At the time when Amascut became the Devourer, I was one of her chief priestesses.
** '''Player:''' So you stopped serving her because of that change?
** '''Neite:''' Not initially. Many of us tolerated her new habits for some time. She went too far though, so we took action.
** '''Player:''' What did you do?
** '''Neite:''' The last of her priestesses gathered and cursed her. Unfortunately, she also cast a spell of her own, condemning us to an eternity of walking Gielinor in her form.
** '''Player:''' So she's a cat then?
** '''Neite:''' She's as much of a cat as Icthlarin is a dog.
** '''Player:''' What curse did you cast upon her?
** '''Neite:''' We trapped her in a human form, limiting her power. We also cursed her to never be willing worshipped again, though I fear that curse has started to wane.
** '''Player:''' So that's why she's scared of cats?
** '''Neite:''' Indeed. There are fewer of us priestesses left now, but we still hold enough power to be quite the problem for her.
** {{tact|other}}
* {{topt|Do you talk to the Sphinx much?}}
** '''Player:''' Do you talk to the Sphinx much?
** '''Neite:''' Not really. She is normally too wrapped up in preserving her immortality to be making conversation.
** '''Player:''' So you don't like her then?
** '''Neite:''' Nothing of the sorts. I have nothing but respect for her.
** '''Player:''' Why is that?
** '''Neite:''' Well, because her immortality is based on the fact that she keeps us cats safe. Her whole existence is dedicated to protecting us.
** '''Player:''' That doesn't seem like much of a life.
** '''Neite:''' True. Life shouldn't be hoarded, but lived. Of course, don't tell her I said that, otherwise I'd have to be on the lookout for a new guardian.

Transcript:Netmaster Kellan.wikitext:
{{Transcript|npc}}
{{Incomplete|Missing subsequent dialogue}}

==Standard dialogue==
* '''Netmaster Kellan:''' Well, what do we have e're? Another laddie lookin' fer old Kellan's deep sea trawlin' expertise?
* '''Player:''' Er.. Maybe?
* '''Netmaster Kellan:''' Well, trawlin's the art of catchin' fish with yer boat. It's the best way to harvest the highest quality fish o' the sea. If ye' be wantin' to learn more, I can tell ye' all ye' need t' know.
* {{tselect|Select an option}}
* {{topt|Who are you?}}
** '''Player:''' Who are you?
** '''Netmaster Kellan:''' The name's Kellan. Used to be a daft-hand at trawlin' back in m'day before the muscles began achin' and the bones started creakin'. These days are better spent helpin you young'uns get yer foot in the trade.
** {{tact|other}}
* {{topt|How do I deep sea trawl?}}
**  '''Player:''' How do I deep sea trawl?
**  '''Netmaster Kellan:''' Well, it all starts with you buildin' a good ol' trawlin' net on yer boat. Rope will do, but linen, hemp and cotton are preferred. The better ye' net, the deeper ye'll be able t' lower it.
**  '''Netmaster Kellan:''' After ye' got a net, ye' need t' find a shoal out at sea. In mos' cases, different shoals 'ave different fish, so make sure yer lookin' for the one ye' want.
**  '''Netmaster Kellan:''' Once ye' find a shoal, it'll probably be on t' move. They travel o'er pretty large distances, but ye'll find 'em stoppin' from time t' time. Once they stop, that be when it's time t' start catchin'.
**  '''Player:''' So that's when I need to lower my net?
**  '''Netmaster Kellan:''' Aye, exactly. However, it's important for ye' to know that different shoals be at different depths, and plen'y of shoals will be swimmin' up and down as well.
**  '''Netmaster Kellan:''' Yer gonna need t' lower the net to the same depth as the shoal, but remember, if the shoal is too deep and yer net ain't up to scratch, yer gonna be all outta luck.
**  '''Player:''' Okay, so I get a good trawling net, find a shoal, wait for it to stop, and then lower the net to the same depth as the shoal. What else?
**  '''Netmaster Kellan:''' If yer wantin' to catch plenty o' fish from a shoal, then yer gonna 'ave to bait it. Best time t' do that is just after it's stopped. For the bait, ye'll be needing lots o' fish offcuts.
**  '''Netmaster Kellan:''' Ye' can get some offcuts by cuttin' up any kind o' fish, but fancier fish like shark an' such will give ye' higher quality ones.
**  '''Player:''' And I'm guessing the fish in some types of shoals are only going to be interested in higher quality offcuts?
**  '''Netmaster Kellan:''' Aye, ye' learn fast, laddie.
**  '''Player:''' So these offcuts... Do I just throw them into the water?
**  '''Netmaster Kellan:''' Well, sort of, but ye'll need t' proper equipment to do it. Specifically, ye'll want to build a chum station on yer boat. They're what ye' use to spread t' offcuts.
**  '''Netmaster Kellan:''' Finally, don't forget that shoals travel o'er big distances. If ye' don't feel the shoals in ye' bones, ye' can build a fathom stone on yer boat. They can help ye' track down a shoals whereabouts.
**  '''Player:''' I see. This is all very different to normal fishing.
**  '''Netmaster Kellan:''' Well, if trawlin's not yer style, laddie, ye' can always cast a rod o'er the side o' the boat and pray they be nibblin', but it's less effective than nets are an' it burns through yer' supply o' bait.
** {{tact|other}}
* {{topt|Where can I deep sea trawl?}}
**  '''Player:''' Where can I deep sea trawl?
**  '''Netmaster Kellan:''' Ye' can do it wherever ye' can find a shoal. They're all across the ocean and yer got different ones fer different fish. I can tell ye' some good places t' find specific ones.
**  '''Netmaster Kellan:''' First up, krill an' haddock are the best shoals for gettin' started. There be a great spot for krill just west o' here in the Great Sound.
**  '''Netmaster Kellan:''' Ye' can also find both krill an' haddock down in t' Unquiet Ocean, around places like Red Rock, the Great Conch and t' like.
**  '''Netmaster Kellan:''' Next ye' got yellowfin an' halibut. There be plen'y o' yellowfin in the Shrouded Ocean, such as near Deepfin Point. Halibut are extra easy! Ye' can find 'em right outside this here port!
**  '''Netmaster Kellan:''' Bluefin are more scattered. Ye' can't really pin 'em down, but I'd try farther south near the waters full of tangled kelp.
**  '''Netmaster Kellan:''' And then ye' got marlin. They can only be found in the' frigid Northern Ocean, but only the best o' boats can survive up there.
**  '''Netmaster Kellan:''' If yer put off by some o' the risks, ye' can try to get lucky. Shoals like t' migrate, an' sometimes them rarer fish mix and mingle with t' other shoals.
** {{tact|other}}
* {{topt|What kind of fish can I catch while trawling?}}
** '''Player:''' What kind of fish can I catch while trawling?
** '''Netmaster Kellan:''' Well, there's giant krill, haddock, yellowfin, halibut, bluefin, and if yer up fer a challenge, the elusive marlin.
** '''Netmaster Kellan:''' These ain't yer normal brand o' fish either. Some say that these are the tastiest fish ye' can get. Some even provide unique effects when ye' eat 'em!
** {{tact|other}}
* {{topt|Do you have any other advice for me?}}
** '''Player:''' Do you have any other advice for me?
** '''Netmaster Kellan:''' I'm sure ol' Kellan can think o' some stuff t' help ye' on yer trawlin' adventures, laddie.
** '''Netmaster Kellan:''' First, ye'll want t' get yer hands on some sturdy fish crates t' hold more fish. Skilled craftsmen can make empty crates out o' camphor logs then ye' pack em full o' ice. Them slayer masters often have ice fer sale.
** '''Netmaster Kellan:''' Second, trawlin' is always better with a good crew by yer side to delegate up the workload. If ye' go it alone, ye'll be trying to man both t' net and chum station at t' same time!
** '''Netmaster Kellan:''' Third, remember that them rarer shoals don't just stay at one depth. Yer gonna find 'em swimmin' up and down. Ye' gotta pay attention and make sure yer net matches their depth.
** '''Netmaster Kellan:''' Finally, don't be forgettin' to bait the shoal when it stops! It'll attract more fish to yer' boat.
** {{tact|other}}
* {{topt|I'd best be off.}}
** '''Player:''' I'd best be off.
** '''Netmaster Kellan:''' Until next time, laddie.
** {{tact|end}}

*** '''Hallak:''' the Menaphite God Pantheon. Elidinis heard the prayers of Nardarine, she took pity on the wandering human and came unto her with water. 'Oh great goddess' exclaimed Nardarine 'I wish not to be involved more in
*** '''Nirrie:''' the wars of the gods for they have caused me so much hardship already, I wish only for a quiet life somewhere'. Elidinis replied 'I will grant this unto thee on the condition that thou swearest to forever pay fealty and

* '''Oath Lord D'rows:''' Good day, adventurer.
* {{topt|Who are you?}}
** '''Player:''' Who are you?

** '''Oath Lord D'rows:''' It is a job I do not take lightly.

** '''Player:''' Which was?
** '''Oath Lord D'rows:''' We Oathbreakers were all once monks of Saradomin but have since seen that his light is false. The founder of this sanctuary had a similar story and that is why we follow in her footsteps.
** '''Player:''' What caused your faith in Saradomin to wane?

** '''Oath Lord D'rows:''' Was there anything else?
** {{tact|other}}
* {{topt|Why are you here?}}
** '''Player:''' Why are you here?
** '''Oath Lord D'rows:''' We've been keeping an eye on Slepe lately. We could sense a darkness building as the citizens fell into their endless slumber.
** '''Oath Lord D'rows:''' Once we'd heard that the sanctuary had been broken into, we came here posthaste.
** '''Player:''' Broken into?
** '''Oath Lord D'rows:''' Indeed. This place was sealed, only to be reopened once Mother had awoken from her deep sleep.
** '''Oath Lord D'rows:''' This nightmarish creature that the siren warned us of has made a home here. That was reason enough for her to unseal the entrance.
** '''Player:''' Oh, um, whose mother? Yours?

** '''Oath Lord D'rows:''' Well, yes, but that fish woman claims every warrior is needed to defeat the Nightmare and that everyone asleep here is at risk.
** '''Oath Lord D'rows:''' We must be strong, adventurer. Be strong for Mother.
** '''Player:''' Okay... Does this creature have treasure? That's kind of a sticking point for me.
** '''Oath Lord D'rows:''' Treasure? This sanctuary is full of old trinkets which the hag has claimed as her own. Kill her and take them, as is the Zamorakian way.
** '''Player:''' Oh yes, the iron price. My specialty.
** {{tact|other}}
* {{topt|Your friends are a quiet bunch.}}
** '''Player:''' Your friends are a quiet bunch.

** '''Player:''' Oh, how come?
** '''Oath Lord D'rows:''' It is the way. When I fall, one of them will take my place as the Oath Lord.
** '''Player:''' No disagreements, that must be nice.
** '''Oath Lord D'rows:''' I never claimed that they can't communicate. They know a rudimentary hand-talk to vent their frustrations with my leadership. Making decisions is easier when no one can shout at you.

** {{tact|other}}
* {{topt|Bye!}}
** '''Player:''' Bye!
** '''Oath Lord D'rows:''' Stay strong, adventurer.

Transcript:Safalaan Hallow.wikitext:
{{transcript|npc}}

==Standard dialogue==
===Initial dialogue===
* '''Safalaan Hallow:''' [player name].
* '''Player:''' Safalaan.
* '''Safalaan Hallow:''' It's strange, this place. From the plants, to the creatures... even the land itself. It's all undeniably horrifying, and yet... there's a certain feeling of peace here.
* '''Safalaan Hallow:''' I wonder if it's the simplicity. There are no politics here. No debates. You don't need to care about good or evil, because there isn't any. Here you can just... be.
* '''Safalaan Hallow:''' Or of course, maybe that's just the monster within me talking.
* '''Player:''' You're no monster, Safalaan.
* '''Safalaan Hallow:''' Are you sure? How do you know I'm not about to try and eat you right now?
* '''Player:''' Er... You are joking right?
* '''Safalaan Hallow:''' Probably... Or am I? Hard to say for sure... You never know when the urge to feed will take hold...
* '''Player:''' Safalaan!
* '''Safalaan Hallow:''' Come on, [player name], look at me. Even other vampyres consider me an abomination... At least let me find some humour in all of this.
* '''Player:''' *hmph* Like you'd be able to eat me anyway. You do remember that I'm the one that finally killed Drakan, right?
* '''Safalaan Hallow:''' In truth, I can still barely believe it. All those years fighting him, and now it's finally all over... It almost doesn't feel real.
* '''Player:''' Well, you were a bit out of it for a fair chunk.
* '''Safalaan Hallow:''' ...
* '''Player:''' Oh, so the humour is only okay when you do it?
* '''Safalaan Hallow:''' Just seems a bit unfair to kick me while I'm down... Maybe I should eat you...
* '''Player:''' It's good to see you haven't changed, Safalaan.
* '''Safalaan Hallow:''' And for as long as I have friends like you, [player name], I hope I never will. Thank you... truly.
* '''Player:''' Like I told you, Safalaan, we're in this together. Anyway, I'll leave you to it, but we'll talk more soon.
* '''Safalaan Hallow:''' Until next time, [player name].
* {{tact|end}}

===Subsequent times===
* '''Player:''' Safalaan. How are things going?
* '''Safalaan Hallow:''' [player name]. I must admit, things are very tiring at the moment. Even with help from mother, controlling this... condition takes a lot of work.
* '''Safalaan Hallow:''' That's before we even get onto the work I've been doing to help Sugadinti with the blood shortages.
* '''Player:''' What have you been doing?
* '''Safalaan Hallow:''' As a wyrd, I hunger far more than a normal vampyre. It... disgusts me, to be honest. However, it does mean I am a perfect test subject for Sugadinti.
* '''Player:''' You're not doing too much, are you?
* '''Safalaan Hallow:''' Perhaps, but I'd prefer to be useful. I find it easier, keeping myself busy. It helps me deal with things. Helps me come to terms with who I am now.
* '''Player:''' Fair enough. You just make sure to let me know if anything gets too much.
* '''Safalaan Hallow:''' Oh I will. As you yourself reminded me, it would be unwise to get on the bad side of the one who finally killed Drakan.
* '''Player:''' Shame I didn't do the same to his sister. If I had, you'd never have been in this position.
* '''Safalaan Hallow:''' Perhaps, or perhaps we'd just all be dead instead. Besides, Vanescula has already been well and truly punished for what she did.
* '''Player:''' Not too eager to forgive her, are you?
* '''Safalaan Hallow:''' Forgive her? Never. But with her in her state and me in mine, she'll fear me for the rest of her days.
* '''Player:''' I suppose there is some justice in that.
* '''Safalaan Hallow:''' Indeed. Now, you'll have to forgive me, [player name], but I believe Sugadinti will have need of me soon. I'll see you later.
* '''Player:''' Until next time, Safalaan.
* {{tact|end}}

Transcript:Shura.wikitext:
{{Transcript|npc}}

==Standard dialogue==
* '''Shura:''' Human.
* {{topt|Tell me about the Nightmare.}}
** '''Player:''' Tell me about the Nightmare.
** '''Shura:''' From the moment I was born, all I ever knew was the Nightmare. Every night she would feast upon us, filling our minds with horrors beyond comprehension.
** '''Shura:''' By day, our warriors would enter her lair in the caves beneath the island. We could not hope to defeat her, we knew that, but our survival was dependent on ensuring she didn't grow too strong.
** '''Shura:''' Here's the thing though. Even now, we know little about her. Before she claimed them, my parents would sometimes tell me a story of her origin.
** '''Shura:''' They told me of a group of shamans who performed an unknown ritual in the hope of gaining great power. The ritual went wrong, though, and instead, they unleashed the Nightmare on this world.
** '''Player:''' Do you believe the story?
** '''Shura:''' I'm not sure to be honest. I suppose it doesn't matter though. We'll likely never know her true origin. But as long as we can defeat her, we don't need to.
** '''Player:''' Defeat her? Using the totems?
** '''Shura:''' Exactly. Thanks to the Nightmare, the caves beneath our home are mostly unexplored. There's all sorts of things down there, provided you're brave enough to enter.
** '''Shura:''' I found the totems deep within the caves. Someone far smarter than you or I had worked out how to make them. But they perished before they could use them against her.
** '''Shura:''' I managed to recover them, and with them, we finally drove her off the island.
** '''Player:''' But she came here.
** '''Shura:''' Yes. And thanks to the Sleeper Plague, she's far stronger than ever before.
** '''Player:''' Do you know where the Sleeper Plague came from?
** '''Shura:''' No. It was here long before the Nightmare apparently. It resurfaced shortly before she arrived. Probably the work of the vampyres.
** '''Shura:''' Is there anything else you need?
** {{tact|other}}
* {{topt|Tell me about yourself.}}
** '''Player:''' Tell me about yourself.
** '''Shura:''' The name's Shura. I come from an island called Ashihama, in the Pincers.
** '''Player:''' The Pincers?
** '''Shura:''' It's a group of islands within the Wushanko Isles, a large archipelago to the far east. Over here I think the area is more commonly known as the Eastern Lands.
** '''Player:''' And you're a siren, right?
** '''Shura:''' That's right. We rarely come this far to the west, the climate is too cold for our tastes. Although while the Nightmare lives, the climate is the least of my worries.
** '''Shura:''' Back home on the other hand, our numbers equal the humans. Sirens live on pretty much every island in the archipelago.
** '''Player:''' So why were you the only one to come here?
** '''Shura:''' We took up arms against the Nightmare because we had to, not because we wanted to. We are a peaceful race, and most were all too eager to lay down their weapons once the Nightmare was gone.
** '''Player:''' So why didn't you?
** '''Shura:''' My kind believe in something called Mo Kal. It means that anything bad that could happen, will happen. The others may have forgotten this, but I have not.
** '''Shura:''' The Nightmare may have left my home, but I won't rest until I know for sure that she can never return.
** '''Shura:''' Is there anything else you need?
** {{tact|other}}
* {{topt|Do you have any of my items?}}
** '''Player:''' Do you have any of my items?
** {{tcond|If the player has no items in Shura's collection:}}
*** '''Shura:''' Doesn't look like it. If I did have any of your items, but you died before collecting them, they'll now be lost.
*** {{tact|end}}
** {{tcond|If the player has items in Shura's collection:}}
*** '''Shura:''' I do. Try to be more careful with them next time.
*** {{tact|opens2=Shura's Item Retrieval Service}}
* {{topt|I'd better get going.}}
** '''Player:''' I'd better get going.
** '''Shura:''' Good luck.
** {{tact|end}}

===When trying to interact with [[The Nightmare]] before talking to her===
* '''Shura:''' Hey! Don't just go poking her without knowing what you're up against. Come talk to me first.
* {{tact|The player walks to Shura.}}
* {{tact|continue}}

===First time talking to her===
* '''Player:''' What's going on here?
* '''Shura:''' Nothing good. This dungeon is tainted and has become the new home of the Nightmare.
* '''Player:''' The Nightmare?
* '''Shura:''' A being of pure darkness. No living creature is safe from her hunger. She feasts upon her victims while they sleep, draining their energy without even needing to touch them.
* '''Shura:''' Those that she feeds upon experience horrifying nightmares, unlike anything you could possibly imagine. Eventually, they become too weak to even wake. Death claims them soon after.
* '''Player:''' Nightmares? Hence the name?
* '''Shura:''' Indeed. Our kind are not always the most creative.
* '''Player:''' So how did she end up here?
* '''Shura:''' For generations, she terrorised the island of Ashihama, my home. I lost a lot of good friends to her. Sometimes, I even thought I would lose myself. For some, the nightmares become too much to bear.
* '''Shura:''' Some of us refused to give in though. Everything has a weakness, including the Nightmare, and eventually we found it. We drove her off the island, but she managed to endure.
* '''Shura:''' The people here are ill, suffering from a deep sleep from which few wake. They call it the Sleeper Plague. The illness made these people easy prey for the Nightmare, so she made this place her new home.
* '''Player:''' And you followed her here?
* '''Shura:''' While she still exists, my home will never be truly safe. Thanks to the Sleeper Plague, her power has grown faster than it ever did on Ashihama. If she is allowed to grow too strong, there won't be any way to stop her.
* '''Shura:''' I've managed to contain her within this section of the dungeon. She has no desire to leave for the moment. She has no need to, after all.
* '''Shura:''' But make no mistake, I won't be able to stop her if she decides to move on.
* '''Player:''' She doesn't look too dangerous at the moment.
* '''Shura:''' Looks can be deceiving. The battle with the Nightmare is a mental one, not a physical one. If you try to take her on, she will pull you into her dream - one where she makes the rules.
* '''Player:''' But if it's a dream, how can it be dangerous?
* '''Shura:''' It's her dream, not yours. Dying in her dream will destroy your mind, killing you in this world as well.
* '''Player:''' Sounds lovely. So how can we stop her?
* '''Shura:''' If you're willing to help, enter her dream and fight to keep her at bay. Our only hope is to prevent her from growing too strong.
* '''Shura:''' You can go in alone, but I wouldn't recommend it. The more support you have, the better your chances.
* '''Player:''' How do I keep her at bay?
* '''Shura:''' There are four totems in the area that can be used to harm her. First, you'll need to take down her shield for the totems to have an effect. Once her shield is down, use your energy to charge up the totems.
* '''Shura:''' She won't sit about while you do this though, so you'll need to take care if you want to survive.
* '''Player:''' And what's in it for me if I do survive?
* '''Shura:''' You mean apart from saving the world? She's claimed many victims over the years. I'm sure she's claimed many items as well. Maybe some of them will be of value to you.
* '''Player:''' Works for me. I'd better get started then.
* '''Shura:''' Good luck. Return to me if you need more information.
* {{tact|end}}

===Right-click Collect===
* {{tcond|If the player has no items in Shura's collection:}}

Transcript:Sister Aseret.wikitext:

==Standard dialogue==
* '''Player:''' Hello!
* '''Sister Aseret:''' Greetings, traveller.
* {{topt|What's with all these Oathbreakers?}}
** '''Player:''' What's with all these Oathbreakers?
** '''Sister Aseret:''' Gah! A bunch of fanatical cultists. Nothing more.
** {{tcond|If the player has not yet defeated The Nightmare:}}
*** '''Player:''' You don't sound impressed?
*** '''Sister Aseret:''' No! Well I wouldn't be, would I? I've spent my whole life dedicated to my sect. I dreamed of one day entering the Sanctuary and finally meeting Mother!
*** '''Sister Aseret:''' Yet instead I'm greeted by this condescending 'Lord' who feels I could try being 'a little more chaotic' for once.
*** '''Player:''' I see...
*** '''Sister Aseret:''' And to top it all off, Mother hasn't awoken at all. I fear she is probably being held captive by this Nightmare, or worse.
*** '''Sister Aseret:''' The only things these oafs are breaking is my head with their silent stares and furious hand-talk.
*** '''Player:''' I'm sorry your day hasn't been going well.
*** '''Sister Aseret:''' Ah... Thank you, traveller. Are you here to fight the Nightmare?
*** '''Player:''' We'll see. Sounds pretty tough.
*** '''Sister Aseret:''' I'll pray for you.
*** {{tact|other}}
** {{tcond|If the player has previously defeated The Nightmare, there is a chance the following branch will be displayed:}}
*** '''Player:''' They seem to be carrying dangerous weapons.
*** '''Sister Aseret:''' Indeed. Speaking of weapons, I assume you have heard of the immensely powerful orbs the Nightmare is protecting?
*** '''Player:''' Yes I have. In fact, I've managed to beat the Nightmare myself.
*** '''Player:''' Anyway, as you've heard of the orbs I assume you've also heard of the even stronger Bashyhammer of Ashihama?
*** '''Sister Aseret:''' The what?
*** '''Player:''' The Smashyhammer of Ashihama.
*** '''Sister Aseret:''' But you just said...
*** '''Player:''' ...Trashyhammer of Ashihama. Yes, I know what I said.
*** '''Sister Aseret:''' Wha-
*** '''Player:''' Slashyhammer?
*** '''Sister Aseret:''' That doesn't even make sense.
*** '''Player:''' Dashyhammer? Mashyhammer?
*** '''Sister Aseret:''' ...
*** '''Player:''' Flashyhammer?
*** '''Sister Aseret:''' Too far. I'm done.
*** {{tact|end}}
* {{topt|What's with the mask?}}
** '''Player:''' What's with the mask?
** '''Sister Aseret:''' These are the masks of the Sisterhood. While symbolic, they also have practical uses.
** '''Player:''' Oh really? What like?
** '''Sister Aseret:''' Herbs can be stored within the beak, masking the smell of death and preventing us from becoming infected.
** '''Player:''' That sounds handy. Can I have one?
** '''Sister Aseret:''' You ask too many questions.
** '''Player:''' Is that a yes?
** '''Sister Aseret:''' It's a no. To wear a mask of the Sisterhood, you need to join the Sisterhood.
** '''Player:''' What is the Sisterhood?
** '''Sister Aseret:''' An ancient order, born right here in Slepe.
** '''Player:''' Well sign me up!
** '''Sister Aseret:''' You lack the qualities we're currently looking for. Perhaps another time.
** {{topt|Tell me more about the Sisterhood.}}
*** '''Player:''' Tell me more about the Sisterhood.

*** '''Sister Aseret:''' However, our leader, a justiciar known as Phosani, saw the truth in Saradomin's teachings and turned away from his false light.
*** '''Sister Aseret:''' Phosani embraced the glory of Zamorak and most of our order did the same. After that, she became known as the Inquisitor, though our order refers to her as 'Mother'.
*** '''Sister Aseret:''' After the order reached enlightenment through Zamorak, we made our home in an abandoned hermitage. Over time, that hermitage grew into the town you see today.
*** '''Player:''' What happened to those that refused to turn away from Saradomin?
*** '''Sister Aseret:''' They were shown the error of their ways through fire and blood.
*** '''Player:''' How wonderful.
*** {{tact|other}}
** {{topt|What's with all these Oathbreakers?}}
*** {{tact|above}}
** {{topt|Bye!}}
*** {{tact|below}}
* {{topt|Bye!}}
** '''Player:''' Bye!
** '''Sister Aseret:''' Be safe, traveller.
** {{tact|end}}

==Rare alternate dialogue==
* '''Player:''' Hello, Smol Heredit.
* '''Smol Heredit:''' Mankind's variation frightens me.
* '''Smol Heredit:''' The way they saw this universe, their modes of impression, differed so greatly from one another that to read their stories, to know their lives, is to wonder if they were not many species in one.
* '''Smol Heredit:''' It was as if they had ranged across the actions of a thousand species and taken them for their own.
* '''Smol Heredit:''' For nearly two thousand years they dreamed in a creative mania without antecedent.
* '''Smol Heredit:''' They looked into the eyes and minds of other species and with their own intellect superseded them.
* '''Smol Heredit:''' They destroyed many, coopted others, and in the space between necessity and carelessness, left some to grow as untended as any species could in the wake of their ubiquity.
* '''Smol Heredit:''' They swarmed across the continents and oceans of a Gielinor they called their own, and shattered it into a billion imbricate worlds.
* '''Smol Heredit:''' And they were, by the twisted jungles of their slaughterhouses, ruthless and aloof beyond measure.
* '''Smol Heredit:''' The worst of us.
* '''Smol Heredit:''' A superpredator.
* '''Smol Heredit:''' A bringer of mass extinction.
* '''Smol Heredit:''' All mountains move and all giants are mountains.
* '''Smol Heredit:''' We rest upon their shoulders.
* '''Smol Heredit:''' The world has grown older, senescent.
* '''Smol Heredit:''' We are chimpanzee, we are gorilla, we are orangutan, and we are baboon and more.
* '''Smol Heredit:''' We are, whether we like it or not, the blood legatees of humanity.
* '''Smol Heredit:''' We are the children of men, but our mistakes will not be their mistakes.
* '''Smol Heredit:''' We are telling a story.
* '''Smol Heredit:''' We are telling a story of life, of what it means to live together in this universe, with vastly different modes of being, of seeing, of knowing.
* '''Smol Heredit:''' Of sharing our own internal worlds with each other and making the universe we live in better for it. The empathy of a mind speaking to another mind, a vastly different mind, and yet each understanding each.
* '''Smol Heredit:''' And if not, if the barriers seem too great, then striving to overcome them.
* '''Smol Heredit:''' Sorrow in what humanity did to this world, in the horrors they unleashed, in their cataclysm of despair, in the tens of thousands of species that will never walk or swim or fly again.
* '''Smol Heredit:''' Extinctions abounded in their wake, and yet look now at this sunbright land, at the joys we have brought to it, to have bound the chaotic climate to our will.
* '''Smol Heredit:''' To have thought deeply of the future of this world, a sense of respect, of shared reverence for it and all who live within it.
* '''Smol Heredit:''' We have strung the close sky with life.
* '''Smol Heredit:''' Be proud.
* '''Smol Heredit:''' And empathy, once limited only to mankind and some few species, now extends across all lands, across all time.
* '''Player:''' ...
* '''Player:''' I'm sorry, but what?!
* {{tact|end}}
